title: kv-cache: refine eviction/defrag heuristics to reduce fragmentation and spillover under mixed workloads (v8)
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: We've observed increased KV cache fragmentation and downstream spillover under mixed sequence-length and multi-tenant workloads. Fragmentation increases memory amplification and causes unexpected paging/spillover leading to tail-latency spikes and OOMs in stressed Dedicated clusters. This PR refines the eviction and defragmentation heuristics (v8) to reduce fragmentation, prefer cheaper spill candidates, and introduce background defrag scheduling with safety controls.

What I changed (high level): unified fragmentation scoring: per-segment free-run-length and dirty-range heuristics; candidate selection now prefers contiguous runs that reduce fragmentation instead of just LRU score; introduced a two-tier eviction path (fast reclaim for hot pressure, careful coalesce+defrag for background reclaim); background defrag worker with adaptive sleep/backoff and CPU budget; paging/spillover threshold split: soft_threshold triggers incremental spill, hard_threshold triggers emergency reclaim/backpressure; added backpressure signal to dispatcher to bias batching away from nodes under severe spill.

Compatibility: Heuristics are implemented as runtime-config knobs (KV_EVICT_MODE, KV_DEFRAG_THRESHOLD, KV_SOFT_PAGING_RATIO) and default to previous safe behavior. Changes are isolated to pkg/serving/kv_cache and have small, well-documented public config surface.

Testing and validation: unit tests for scoring and candidate selection, integration test that reproduces mixed-length fragmentation trace and verifies <12% spillover regression vs baseline, bench harness (examples/benchmarks/kv_frag_bench.py) shows 5-12% reduction in spillover rate and 4-9% improvement in average token latency in high-mix traces. CI includes stress runs, and we validated on a small Dedicated canary fleet behind feature flag before merge.

Rollout plan: feature gated by KV_EVICT_MODE=v8. Start canary 5% on release/2026-02 for 48h, monitor kv.spillover.rate, kv.fragmentation.p95, and OOM events. If stable, increase to 50% then 100% and backport a minimal config to release branch.

Notes: this PR focuses on heuristics. Future work will look at compact-on-allocate to further reduce fragmentation and explore kernel-level pinned defrag operations where supported.
commits_summary: 7 commits: initial heuristic refactor; fragmentation scoring implementation; background defrag worker + tests; paging threshold split + dispatcher backpressure; docs/rfc; bench harness; CI adjustments and flakiness fixes.
review_comments: Miguel Santos (request changes): We need to ensure the background defrag worker can't cause CPU contention on small hosts — please add a CPU budget knob and a conservative default.
Author (Aisha): Added KV_DEFRAG_CPU_BUDGET and a measured default (5% of a vCPU) and updated tests to assert budget respected.
Evelyn Zhang (approve): Verified integration stress runs on canary; fragmentation p95 dropped and spillover events reduced; recommend squash-and-merge.
Tomás Rivera: Left one minor nit about metric labels in metrics.go (changed kv.fragmentation -> kv.fragmentation.bytes) — done.
ci_checks: perf: perf-bench (kv_frag_bench) - baseline vs v8: pass (improved)
merge_outcome: Squash and merge by Evelyn Zhang after approvals. Backported a minimal config change to release/2026-02 via cherrypick (pr-73296).
release_notes: Improves KV cache eviction and defragmentation heuristics to reduce memory amplification and spillover under mixed sequence-length workloads. Expect fewer OOMs, reduced spillover rates (5-12% in benchmarks), and improved token latency in high-mix traces. Exposes tunable knobs: KV_EVICT_MODE, KV_DEFRAG_THRESHOLD, KV_DEFRAG_CPU_BUDGET, KV_SOFT_PAGING_RATIO.
